component.name: PairDesk
component.summary: Control this computer from your phone

description.p: PairDesk turns your Android phone into a remote for this computer. Pair once by scanning a code; after that your phone connects by itself whenever you open the app.

ul.li: Touchpad and keyboard: move, click, scroll, drag and type
See the screen and control it with touch, like a touchpad
Shortcuts and key combinations, media and volume keys
Open apps, lock, sleep, restart or shut down
Copy and paste between phone and computer, send files both ways
Works on the same Wi-Fi, or from anywhere with Tailscale

description.p: Connections are encrypted and only phones you paired can connect. Nothing goes through a PairDesk server: there isn't one.

screenshot.caption: Pair your phone by scanning the code

description.p: The phone no longer drops a connection that is still alive: it waits longer for the computer, does not mistake its own sleep for a silent computer, and reconnects by itself when the link really breaks.

Connecting from another network now works with nothing to set up: the PairDesk relay is live and used by default. You can also reach a computer through a port forward on your own router by typing its name or address into the phone.

Computers stay reachable away from home: PairDesk now tells phones straight away when its addresses change, so turning Tailscale on reaches a phone that was paired before it. On Windows it can write firewall rules for every kind of network, which is what stopped Tailscale connections getting through. The phone app also installs its own updates now.

Pair by sending a link instead of scanning the QR code. "Get help" lets someone see and control your screen for a while, with power, files and sound kept off. When the phone can't reach the computer directly, it now connects through the PairDesk relay, still encrypted end to end.
Talk and listen at the same time, like a call, with echo cancelling on both sides.
Two-way sound: hear the computer on the phone, talk through the computer's speakers, and (if allowed) hear its microphone.
Fixes the phone app closing when Smooth screen view is on. A new look with separate screens, and on Windows, PairDesk opens in its own window instead of the browser.
Smoother screen view (H.264 video). On Windows: the lock screen, the sign-in screen and administrator prompts can be used from the phone.
Installers for Windows and Linux, automatic updates, and a proper icon.
Clipboard and file transfer between phone and computer.
See and control the screen from the phone.
